\textbf{Dynamic Stopping Distance (\(d_{\text{stop}}\))} & The total
physical clearance required to bring a moving mass to a complete halt
(\(d_{\text{stop}}(v) = v \cdot \tau_{\text{latency}} + \frac{v^2}{2 a_{\max}} + \delta_{\text{margin}}\)),
combining linear reaction latency displacement with quadratic braking
travel. & Chapter~\ref{sec-body}, Chapter~\ref{sec-enforcement} \\
\textbf{Inevitable Collision State (ICS)} & A physical state \((x, v)\)
from which no admissible control trajectory exists that can prevent a
collision with obstacles or environment boundaries, given the robot's
finite acceleration limits \(a_{\max}\). & Chapter~\ref{sec-body},
Chapter~\ref{sec-planning}, Chapter~\ref{sec-enforcement} \\
\textbf{Dynamic Fallback Ladder (MRM)} & A 4-tier structured escalation
protocol executed by the real-time supervisor when anomalies occur:
Level 1 (Minimal Intervention QP), Level 2 (Category 2 Position Hold),
Level 3 (Category 1 Controlled Dynamic Stop), Level 4 (Category 0 Safe
Torque Off with spring-applied mechanical brakes). &
Chapter~\ref{sec-enforcement}, Chapter~\ref{sec-intervention} \\
\textbf{Category 0 Stop (IEC 60204-1)} & An uncontrolled emergency stop
achieved by immediately disconnecting electrical power to machine
actuators, allowing gravity or spring-applied friction brakes to
dissipate energy. & Chapter~\ref{sec-body},
Chapter~\ref{sec-enforcement} \\
\textbf{Category 1 Stop (IEC 60204-1)} & A controlled stop where power
is maintained to actuators to execute a maximum-deceleration dynamic
brake trajectory until standstill, followed by complete power cutoff. &
Chapter~\ref{sec-body}, Chapter~\ref{sec-enforcement} \\
\textbf{Category 2 Stop (IEC 60204-1)} & A controlled stop where power
remains continuously supplied to machine actuators to maintain an active
position hold against external gravity or process loads. &
Chapter~\ref{sec-body}, Chapter~\ref{sec-enforcement} \\
\textbf{Envelope Trichotomy} & The formal safety case principle
partitioning runtime state queries into \emph{known-true} (verified
safe, permit action), \emph{known-false} (boundary breach, immediate
trip), and \emph{unknown} (epistemic uncertainty, sensor dropout).
Crucially, \textbf{unknown must be treated as strictly outside the
envelope}, triggering immediate degraded control. &
Chapter~\ref{sec-release} \\
\textbf{Claim-Argument-Evidence (CAE)} & A formal assurance framework
structuring safety cases: top-level claims are broken down into logical
sub-arguments supported by empirical test evidence from
hardware-in-the-loop and in-situ fault injection records. &
Chapter~\ref{sec-release} \\
\textbf{Residual-Claims Register} & An auditable engineering ledger
documenting every operational claim that cannot be empirically verified
by testing or proven by software contracts, binding each residual risk
to active mechanical containment and accountable human ownership. &
Chapter~\ref{sec-frontier} \\
\textbf{Detectorless Failure Mode} & A catastrophic physical failure
mechanism that produces no detectable change in electronic telemetry
before physical damage occurs (e.g., thermal rotor demagnetization,
subsurface gear pitting, piezoresistive sensor diaphragm fatigue).
Requires physical proof-testing rather than software monitoring. &
Chapter~\ref{sec-frontier} \\
\textbf{Covariate Shift Flywheel} & The vicious cycle in imitation
learning where compounding execution errors push the robot into
unfamiliar states outside demonstration support, triggering larger
errors that steer the machine directly toward hazards
(\(O(T^2 \epsilon)\) error accumulation). & Chapter~\ref{sec-data},
Chapter~\ref{sec-training} \\
\textbf{Demonstration Provenance Tuple} & The 4-stream action logging
protocol
\((a_{\text{req}}, a_{\text{cmd}}, a_{\text{enf}}, a_{\text{meas}})\)
that distinguishes intentional human teleop commands
(\(a_{\text{req}}\)) from kinematic transformations
(\(a_{\text{cmd}}\)), safety governor clamps (\(a_{\text{enf}}\)), and
structural compliance/backlash (\(a_{\text{meas}}\)). &
Chapter~\ref{sec-data} \\

\chapter*{Cross-Disciplinary Translation
Lexicon}\label{sec-appendix-lexicon}
\addcontentsline{toc}{chapter}{Cross-Disciplinary Translation Lexicon}

\markboth{Cross-Disciplinary Translation Lexicon}{Cross-Disciplinary
Translation Lexicon}

Physical AI sits at the intersection of four distinct engineering
traditions: \textbf{Modern Deep Learning (AI)}, \textbf{Classical
Robotics \& Non-Linear Control}, \textbf{Real-Time Embedded Systems \&
Silicon Architecture}, and \textbf{Safety-Critical Systems Assurance}.

Because each discipline developed its own vocabulary over decades,
engineers from different backgrounds frequently use the same words to
mean completely different things---or use different words for the exact
same underlying physical concept. This appendix serves as a
cross-disciplinary Rosetta Stone.

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\section*{2. False Friends: Words That Cause Catastrophic
Misunderstandings}\label{false-friends-words-that-cause-catastrophic-misunderstandings}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{2. False Friends: Words That Cause
Catastrophic Misunderstandings}

\markright{2. False Friends: Words That Cause Catastrophic
Misunderstandings}

\subsection*{``Deterministic''}\label{deterministic}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{``Deterministic''}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{In Deep Learning:} Setting \texttt{torch.manual\_seed(42)} and
  \texttt{cudnn.deterministic\ =\ True} so the matrix multiplication
  forward pass produces bit-identical tensor values across offline runs.
\item
  \textbf{In Embedded \& Real-Time Systems:} Guaranteeing that every
  periodic task completes in hardware time \(t \le T_{\text{deadline}}\)
  with bounded jitter (\(<1\,\mu\text{s}\)), regardless of CPU cache
  misses, interrupt storms, or bus contention. \emph{An algorithm that
  always outputs the same tensor 10 milliseconds too late is
  non-deterministic in physical systems.}
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{``Real-Time''}\label{real-time}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{``Real-Time''}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{In Web \& Cloud Software:} A web service or UI that updates
  within \(100\text{--}200\text{ ms}\) (``real-time chat'', ``real-time
  streaming''), where occasional delays cause dropped frames or
  buffering spinners without danger.
\item
  \textbf{In Physical AI Systems:} Hard deadline determinism where
  missing a single \(1.0\text{ ms}\) execution deadline
  (\(1000\text{ Hz}\)) produces an inverter current loop runaway,
  mechanical resonance, or irreversible collision.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{``State''}\label{state}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{``State''}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{In Deep Learning:} The internal hidden activations of an RNN,
  the latent state of an autoencoder, or the Key-Value (KV) cache of an
  attention layer (\(\mathbf{h}_t \in \mathbb{R}^d\)). It has no
  explicit spatial units.
\item
  \textbf{In Robotics \& Physics:} The complete, physically grounded
  coordinate representation of the mechanical system
  (\(\mathbf{x} = [\mathbf{q}^T, \dot{\mathbf{q}}^T]^T \in \mathbb{R}^{2n}\))
  representing positions in meters, angles in radians, velocities in
  \(\text{m/s}\), and temperatures in Kelvin.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{``Latency''}\label{latency}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{``Latency''}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{In Machine Learning Benchmarks:} The average execution time of
  \texttt{model.forward()} on an isolated GPU under synthetic batching
  (\(P_{50} \approx 15\text{ ms}\)), ignoring camera frame exposure, OS
  scheduler queueing, and DMA memory bus transfer.
\item
  \textbf{In Physical AI:} The \textbf{Spatial Information Age}
  (\(\tau_{\text{age}}\)): the total wall-clock duration from the photon
  striking the camera photodiode at exposure midpoint
  \(t_{\text{exp}}/2\) to the instant mechanical torque is exerted on
  the physical environment. In real hardware, \(\tau_{\text{age}}\) is
  often \(3\times\) to \(5\times\) larger than the GPU forward pass.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{``Safe''}\label{safe}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{``Safe''}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{In AI Alignment:} The model avoids generating toxic language,
  hate speech, or copyrighted text.
\item
  \textbf{In Physical Systems:} The system maintains forward invariance
  with respect to physical kinetic boundaries (\(h(\mathbf{x}) \ge 0\)),
  guaranteeing that actuator torque, velocity, and deceleration remain
  mathematically incapable of inflicting mechanical trauma or structural
  destruction.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{``Robustness''}\label{robustness}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{``Robustness''}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{In Deep Learning:} Maintaining classification accuracy under
  adversarial pixel noise (\(\ell_\infty\) epsilon-balls) or image
  corruption (fog, blur).
\item
  \textbf{In Control \& Embedded Systems:} Maintaining closed-loop
  stability across plant parameter variations (gain/phase margins,
  \(\mathcal{H}_\infty\) norm bounds) and hardware physical resilience
  against electrical noise, bus EMI, power supply voltage droop, and
  thermal throttling.
\end{itemize}

\subsection*{``Policy''}\label{policy}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{``Policy''}

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{In Reinforcement Learning:} The parameterized neural network
  \(\pi_\theta(a \mid s)\) mapping states to action distributions.
\item
  \textbf{In Systems Engineering:} The top-level administrative or
  operational policy governing access rights, operator qualifications,
  and deployment sign-offs.
\end{itemize}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\section*{3. Practical Translation Guides for
Students}\label{practical-translation-guides-for-students}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{3. Practical Translation Guides for
Students}

\markright{3. Practical Translation Guides for Students}

\subsection*{If you are coming from Computer Science / Deep
Learning:}\label{if-you-are-coming-from-computer-science-deep-learning}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{If you are coming from Computer
Science / Deep Learning:}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Forget \texttt{malloc()} on the fast loop:} You cannot
  allocate dynamic memory or resize lists inside a \(1000\text{ Hz}\)
  control loop. Heap fragmentation causes random multi-millisecond
  pauses that crash physical robots.
\item
  \textbf{Your model is an unprivileged proposer:} A neural network must
  never have direct write access to motor registers. It proposes intent;
  a deterministic mathematical filter running on bare metal permits,
  clamps, or rejects the command.
\item
  \textbf{Loss \(= 0\) in simulation does not mean it works:} Physics
  engines approximate contact dynamics as linear complementarity
  problems (LCP). Real contact friction is non-smooth,
  stiction-dominated, and thermally variable.
\item
  \textbf{Bandwidth matters more than FLOPS:} Streaming multi-gigabyte
  neural weights from LPDDR5 DRAM on edge SoCs creates a memory wall
  (\(t_{\text{stream}} = M_{\text{weights}} / B_{\text{mem}}\)) that
  limits inference cadence, regardless of how many TFLOPS the NPU matrix
  core claims.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{If you are coming from Mechanical Engineering / Control
Theory:}\label{if-you-are-coming-from-mechanical-engineering-control-theory}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{If you are coming from Mechanical
Engineering / Control Theory:}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Uncertainty is multimodal:} Classical Kalman filters assume
  unimodal Gaussian noise. Perception models in the real world face
  discrete semantic hypotheses (e.g., an object is either in front of or
  behind a partition), requiring multimodal policy representations
  (Diffusion / Mixture Density Networks).
\item
  \textbf{You cannot write down the world dynamics \(f(\mathbf{x})\) for
  an unconstrained kitchen or highway:} Analytical ODEs work for steel
  linkages in a factory cell, but fail when interacting with deformable
  objects, varying lighting, and open-world human behavior. Deep models
  provide the semantic perception front-end that classical control
  lacks.
\item
  \textbf{Control Barrier Functions are the bridge:} You do not have to
  discard control theory when using deep learning. Instead, treat the
  learned policy as a nominal reference generator
  \(\mathbf{u}_{\text{ref}}\) and use a Control Barrier Function
  (CBF-QP) as an active safety filter that minimally adjusts
  \(\mathbf{u}\) only when boundary invariants are threatened.
\end{enumerate}

\subsection*{If you are coming from Embedded Systems / Electrical
Engineering:}\label{if-you-are-coming-from-embedded-systems-electrical-engineering}
\addcontentsline{toc}{subsection}{If you are coming from Embedded
Systems / Electrical Engineering:}

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{AI compute is dynamic and stochastic:} You cannot treat neural
  inference like a fixed-cycle DSP FIR filter. Execution time varies
  based on image content, caching, and thermal throttling. You must
  design asynchronous two-speed architectures with expiring leases to
  absorb timing jitter safely.
\item
  \textbf{Data provenance is as critical as voltage integrity:} Logging
  teleoperation data without tracking operator response delays
  (\(340\text{ ms}\)) or safety governor clamps poisons training
  pipelines via covariate shift.
\item
  \textbf{Memory crossbars are a shared resource:} When an NPU bursts
  \(25.6\text{ GB/s}\) of DRAM traffic during a vision transformer
  forward pass, it can starve real-time CPU DMA channels unless hardware
  AXI Quality of Service (QoS) bus arbitration is configured.
\end{enumerate}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\section*{3. Actuator Transmission Mechanics \& Reflected
Inertia}\label{actuator-transmission-mechanics-reflected-inertia}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{3. Actuator Transmission Mechanics \&
Reflected Inertia}

\markright{3. Actuator Transmission Mechanics \& Reflected Inertia}

In physical actuation, a motor's rotor inertia \(J_{\text{rotor}}\) is
amplified by the square of the gear reduction ratio \(N\):

\[J_{\text{eff}} = J_{\text{load}} + N^2 J_{\text{rotor}}\]

\section*{4. Power Delivery Network (PDN) \& Voltage
Droop}\label{power-delivery-network-pdn-voltage-droop}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{4. Power Delivery Network (PDN) \&
Voltage Droop}

\markright{4. Power Delivery Network (PDN) \& Voltage Droop}

When a deep neural network accelerator switches from an idle state to
full-load matrix tensor computation, the step current demand
\(\Delta I\) creates a transient voltage droop across the power
distribution network:

\[\Delta V_{\text{droop}} = L_{\text{trace}} \frac{dI}{dt} + R_{\text{trace}} \Delta I\]

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{The Brownout Risk:} If an edge GPU draws a
  \(\Delta I = 80\text{ A}\) current step in \(10\text{ ns}\) across an
  unconditioned parasitic inductance
  \(L_{\text{trace}} = 0.5\text{ nH}\), the transient droop
  \(\Delta V = 40.0\text{ V}\) can collapse a shared \(48\text{ V}\) DC
  bus below the minimum operating threshold of the microcontroller's
  low-dropout (LDO) regulator (\(<3.3\text{ V}\)), triggering a local
  processor reset.
\item
  \textbf{Architectural Mitigation:} Physical AI systems must employ
  galvanic DC-DC power isolation and dedicated bulk decoupling
  capacitors
  (\(C_{\text{decouple}} \ge \frac{\Delta I \cdot \Delta t}{\Delta V_{\text{allowable}}}\))
  between cognitive accelerators and real-time microcontroller buses.
\end{itemize}

\begin{center}\rule{0.5\linewidth}{0.5pt}\end{center}

\section*{5. Actuator Thermal Rise \& Resistance
Drift}\label{actuator-thermal-rise-resistance-drift}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{5. Actuator Thermal Rise \& Resistance
Drift}

\markright{5. Actuator Thermal Rise \& Resistance Drift}

The electrical resistance of copper motor windings increases linearly
with operating temperature:

\[R_{\text{winding}}(T) = R_0 \left( 1 + \alpha_{\text{Cu}} (T - T_0) \right)\]

where \(\alpha_{\text{Cu}} \approx 0.00393\text{ K}^{-1}\) at
\(T_0 = 20^\circ\text{C}\).

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Consequence for Control:} As a motor heats from
  \(20^\circ\text{C}\) to its maximum thermal limit
  (\(120^\circ\text{C}\)), coil resistance increases by \(+39.3\%\).
  Under voltage-mode control, the achievable phase current and output
  torque drop proportionally by \(28.2\%\), violating nominal kinematic
  reachability assumptions unless closed-loop Field-Oriented Current
  Control (FOC) is enforced at \(>10\text{ kHz}\).
\end{itemize}

\textbf{Uber ATG Tempe Crash} (Mar 2018) & Autonomous Test Vehicle

(\(d_{\text{stop}}\)). & Chapter~\ref{sec-boundary},
Chapter~\ref{sec-brain}, Chapter~\ref{sec-intervention},
Chapter~\ref{sec-release} \\
\textbf{Tesla Autopilot Williston Crash} (May 2016) & Semi-Autonomous
Highway Autopilot & Monocular vision saturated against bright midday
sky; radar reflection rejected as overhead sign & System lacked
cross-modal sensor voting and failed to enforce human gaze attention
invariants & Sensor fusion must explicitly bound epistemic uncertainty;
vision cannot be assumed universally valid under high-dynamic-range
illumination. & Chapter~\ref{sec-perception},
Chapter~\ref{sec-intervention} \\
\textbf{Autonomous Gantry Milling Collision} (Industrial Autopsy) &
5-Axis Heavy CNC Gantry Milling Center & Flash trace logging triggered
high-priority DMA bursts across shared AHB crossbar, starving real-time
SPI bus & Emergency stop task suffered \(600\,\mu\text{s}\) bus
contention, missing \(3.0\text{ ms}\) deceleration deadline &
Safety-critical enforcer code and I/O registers must be isolated in
zero-contention Data Tightly-Coupled Memory (DTCM). &
Chapter~\ref{sec-nervous}, Chapter~\ref{sec-enforcement},
Chapter~\ref{sec-placement} \\
\textbf{Gas Turbine Hydraulic Manifold Rupture} (Energy Plant) &
Closed-Loop Fuel Manifold Pressure Regulator & Low-pass anti-aliasing
filter added \(40\text{ ms}\) phase lag to pressure telemetry, causing
PI controller windup & Control loop lacked dynamic saturation clamping
and rate-of-rise barrier certificates & Low-pass filtering trades noise
reduction for phase lag; transport latency consumes physical stability
margin. & Chapter~\ref{sec-body}, Chapter~\ref{sec-nervous} \\
\textbf{Mars Climate Orbiter Disintegration} (Sep 1999) & Interplanetary
Spacecraft Trajectory Controller & Ground software emitted angular
momentum thruster impulses in pound-force seconds
(\(\text{lbf}\cdot\text{s}\)), while onboard software expected
Newton-seconds (\(\text{N}\cdot\text{s}\)) & Lack of statically typed
dimensional units and coordinate frame contracts in IPC schemas & Every
data structure crossing an interface must explicitly bind physical SI
units and reference frames into immutable schemas. &
Chapter~\ref{sec-data}, Chapter~\ref{sec-perception},
Chapter~\ref{sec-intent} \\
\textbf{Therac-25 Radiation Overdoses} (1985--1987) & Medical Linear
Accelerator & Microsecond operator race conditions and arithmetic
counter overflows bypassed software position checks & Software-only
interlocks replaced physical mechanical interlock switches on the
turntable & Software decision logic cannot replace independent hardware
break circuits and physical trip zones. &
Chapter~\ref{sec-enforcement} \\
\textbf{Ariane 5 Flight 501 Destruction} (Jun 1996) & Heavy Space Launch
Vehicle & 64-bit floating-point horizontal bias converted to 16-bit
signed integer without overflow protection & Reused flight software
emitted diagnostic dump onto shared 1553 bus, interpreted as valid
flight guidance & Reused software components must have explicit
precondition assertions; shared communication buses require strict
spatial and temporal isolation. & Chapter~\ref{sec-placement} \\
\textbf{Boeing 737 MAX MCAS Fatal Crashes} (2018--2019) & Commercial Jet
Transport Flight Control & Single unvalidated Angle-of-Attack (AoA)
sensor vane failure repeatedly triggered automated nose-down trim & Lack
of cross-channel sensor validation; lack of cockpit annunciation; MCAS
overrode pilot control column inputs & Automated flight software must
not possess unmediated authority to overpower physical human control
forces without explicit authorization and disengagement. &
Chapter~\ref{sec-intervention} \\
\textbf{Airbus A320 Warsaw Runway Overrun} (Sep 1993) & Commercial Jet
Aircraft Braking System & Flight computers required simultaneous squat
switch compression and wheel spin-up to confirm ground contact &
Aquaplaning prevented both sensor conditions; flight computer locked out
pilot manual braking and thrust reversers & Rigid boolean software
interlocks must not lock out human emergency intervention during dynamic
edge-case scenarios. & Chapter~\ref{sec-intervention} \\
\textbf{Toyota Unintended Acceleration} (2007--2010) & Electronic
Throttle Control System (ETCS-i) & Single-Event Upset or stack overflow
killed the real-time throttle control task (\texttt{Task\_Throttle}) &
Hardware watchdog was unconditionally kicked by background OS task; dead
throttle task left engine locked at wide-open throttle & Hardware
watchdogs must monitor task-specific progress tokens across all
real-time tasks, not generic CPU liveness. &
Chapter~\ref{sec-verification} \\
\textbf{Space Shuttle Challenger Disaster} (Jan 1986) & Solid Rocket
Booster (SRB) Field Joint & Launch temperature of \(31^\circ\text{F}\)
exceeded Viton O-ring glass transition temperature, delaying resilience
recovery & Engineering management normalized secondary blowby as
acceptable risk under schedule pressure & Statistical survival of past
out-of-envelope operations does not expand certified physical design
envelopes (\emph{normalization of deviance}). &
Chapter~\ref{sec-release} \\
\textbf{Deepwater Horizon BOP Containment Failure} (Apr 2010) & Subsea
Blowout Preventer (BOP) Blind Shear Rams & High-velocity blowout flow
caused drill pipe Euler buckling, deflecting pipe laterally against
casing wall & Blind shear rams were designed only for centered pipe;
pressure telemetry reported nominal actuation while pipe jammed
unsevered & Observational indistinguishability (\(y_A \equiv y_B\))
renders detectorless failure modes invisible to software, requiring
structural containment and physical proof-tests. &
Chapter~\ref{sec-frontier} \\
\textbf{Apollo 11 Radar Cycle Stealing} (Jul 1969) & Apollo Guidance
Computer (AGC) Lunar Module & Rendezvous radar in manual slew flooded
AGC with 800-Hz asynchronous reference pulses (\(15\%\) CPU stolen) &
Priority-scheduled core memory dropped low-priority display tasks to
preserve throttle/thruster control cycles & Deterministic fixed-priority
scheduling and graceful task shedding preserve real-time control
deadlines under bus overload. & Chapter~\ref{sec-verification} \\
\end{longtable}

for Control Barrier Function (CBF-QP) filters in
Chapter~\ref{sec-enforcement}. \\

foundation for the \textbf{Astronomical Exposure Wall} and deductive
Claim-Argument-Evidence safety cases. \\

\textbf{Stop Category 0:} Immediate power cutoff (Safe Torque Off /
mechanical brake drop)• \textbf{Stop Category 1:} Controlled
deceleration to stop with power on, then cutoff• \textbf{Stop Category
2:} Controlled position hold with power maintained & Defines the formal
3-tier physical fallback actions executed by the enforcer during anomaly
escalation in Chapter~\ref{sec-enforcement}. \\

\chapter*{Heterogeneous Dual-Brain SoC Reference
Architecture}\label{sec-appendix-heterogeneous-soc}
\addcontentsline{toc}{chapter}{Heterogeneous Dual-Brain SoC Reference
Architecture}

\markboth{Heterogeneous Dual-Brain SoC Reference
Architecture}{Heterogeneous Dual-Brain SoC Reference Architecture}

This appendix defines the canonical reference architecture for
heterogeneous dual-brain edge systems in Physical AI. It specifies the
hardware topology, core partitioning, inter-processor communication
(IPC) protocols, and hardware safety watchdog contracts that separate
unprivileged stochastic policy deliberation from deterministic real-time
safety enforcement.

\section*{Dual-Brain System Topology}\label{dual-brain-system-topology}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Dual-Brain System Topology}

\markright{Dual-Brain System Topology}

\lettrine{I}{n} an embodied machine, cognitive deliberation and
mechanical actuation operate in fundamentally incompatible timing and
determinism domains. The dual-brain architecture bridges this divide by
mapping functional roles onto asymmetric processing domains on a shared
System-on-Chip (SoC) or coupled compute module:

{\def\LTcaptype{none} % do not increment counter
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Processor Subsystem
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Architectural Core and OS
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Primary Systems Role and Execution Contract
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\textbf{Application Processor (MPU)} & Multi-core 64-bit Application
CPURich OS (Embedded Linux / RT-Linux) & \textbf{Untrusted Proposal
Service:} Runs multimodal perception backbones, foundation models, ROS 2
stacks, and generative trajectory planners; emits timestamped, expiring
candidate proposals (\(p_t\)). \\
\textbf{Real-Time Safety Controller (MCU)} & Deterministic
Microcontroller (ARM Cortex-M / RISC-V)Bare-Metal / Hard RTOS (Zephyr /
FreeRTOS) & \textbf{Trusted Permission Authority:} Runs deterministic
\(1000\text{ Hz}\) control loops, Control Barrier Function safety
filters (\(h(x) \ge 0\)), dynamic stopping enforcers
(\(d_{\text{stop}}\)), and hardware PWM/timer registers. \\
\textbf{Inter-Processor Link (IPC)} & Shared SRAM Mailbox \& Hardware
SemaphoreRPMSG / OpenAMP Framework & Zero-copy lock-free circular ring
buffers with atomic sequence counters, cache-coherent headers, and
hardware mailbox interrupts. \\
\end{longtable}
}

\section*{Hardware Resource
Partitioning}\label{hardware-resource-partitioning}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Hardware Resource Partitioning}

\markright{Hardware Resource Partitioning}

{\def\LTcaptype{none} % do not increment counter
\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 4\tabcolsep) * \real{0.3333}}@{}}
\toprule\noalign{}
\begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Subsystem
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Application Processor (MPU)
\end{minipage} & \begin{minipage}[b]{\linewidth}\raggedright
Real-Time Safety Controller (MCU)
\end{minipage} \\
\midrule\noalign{}
\endhead
\bottomrule\noalign{}
\endlastfoot
\textbf{Core Architecture} & Multi-core Out-of-Order Application CPU +
NPU/GPU & Deterministic In-Order Microcontroller (Zero-Wait-State) \\
\textbf{Operating System} & Embedded Linux (Preempt-RT / Debian / Yocto)
& Bare-Metal Firmware / Hard Real-Time OS \\
\textbf{Memory Subsystem} & 2 GB to 32 GB LPDDR4/LPDDR5 DRAM (Shared) &
256 KB to 1 MB On-Chip SRAM (TCM, Zero-Wait-State) \\
\textbf{Memory Management} & Virtual memory, TLB, demand paging &
Physical addressing only, zero dynamic allocation (\texttt{malloc}
prohibited) \\
\textbf{Execution Determinism} & Best-effort with tail jitter
(\(P_{99} \approx 20\text{--}80\text{ ms}\)) & Hard real-time cycle
predictability (WCET bounded, jitter \(< 1\,\mu\text{s}\)) \\
\textbf{Physical I/O Authority} & High-speed buses: MIPI CSI-2, USB 3.0,
PCIe, GbE & Dedicated safety I/O: Timer PWM, Quadrature Encoders,
Hardware E-Stop GPIO \\
\end{longtable}
}

\section*{Shared Memory RPMSG Message
Contract}\label{shared-memory-rpmsg-message-contract}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Shared Memory RPMSG Message Contract}

\markright{Shared Memory RPMSG Message Contract}

The application processor transmits timestamped intent proposals to the
real-time safety controller over non-blocking shared SRAM mailboxes
using the Remote Processor Messaging (RPMSG) protocol. The shared
message schema (\texttt{PhysicalAgent\_IntentProposal\_t}) enforces a
packed binary layout across cores:

\begin{longtable}[]{@{}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2500}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2500}}
  >{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{(\linewidth - 6\tabcolsep) * \real{0.2500}}

\section*{Hardware Safety Watchdog
Protocol}\label{hardware-safety-watchdog-protocol}
\addcontentsline{toc}{section}{Hardware Safety Watchdog Protocol}

\markright{Hardware Safety Watchdog Protocol}

The real-time controller monitors the application processor via a
dedicated hardware countdown watchdog and heartbeat protocol:

\begin{enumerate}
\def\labelenumi{\arabic{enumi}.}
\tightlist
\item
  \textbf{Heartbeat Packet:} The application processor must transmit an
  authenticated heartbeat packet every
  \(\tau_{\text{ping}} \le 10\text{ ms}\).
\item
  \textbf{Watchdog Timeout:} If the real-time controller receives no
  valid heartbeat for \(\tau_{\text{timeout}} = 50\text{ ms}\), an
  independent hardware timer triggers a Non-Maskable Interrupt (NMI).
\item
  \textbf{Hardware Action:} The real-time controller immediately
  de-asserts motor gate driver enable lines and transitions inverter
  power stages into a deterministic safe stop (Category 1 / Safe Torque
  Off) within \(250\,\mu\text{s}\).
\end{enumerate}
